claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance in air at high temperature.
PVD or ALD can produce a thin protective Al2O3 coating on cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The deposited alumina coating will be continuous and dense.
A continuous, dense alumina layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The alumina coating will remain stable and intact in air at 1000 °C for 100 hours.
The deposited alumina coating forms a thermally grown oxide barrier during high-temperature exposure.
The alumina barrier prevents oxygen from penetrating into the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Suppressing oxygen ingress minimizes oxidation-induced microstructural degradation.
Alumina-coated HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit significantly less surface oxidation than uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure in air at 1000 °C for 100 hours.
The coating will preserve the alloy's original room-temperature tensile ductility after high-temperature exposure.
The coating will preserve the alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
The PVD or ALD process may introduce residual stresses or surface anomalies that adversely affect long-term fatigue or other mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies a pre-deposited PVD/ALD alumina coating, whereas the mechanism calls it a thermally grown oxide barrier. A deposited coating and a thermally grown oxide are distinct formation routes, and no conversion or additional oxide-growth step is explained.

The predicted outcome refers to retaining the original yield strength and ductility under high-temperature conditions, but the stated original ductility is a room-temperature value and the boundary later places ductility testing at room temperature.
